parts.part: excavated area of the Harappan settlement (house platforms and drains)
parts.layout_phase: Sub-period II A, structural Phase I (first of the four structural phases of II A)
parts.what_was_built: Rao found no fortification and could not trace streets: 'It was also not possible to ascertain the lay-out of the streets and alleys of the Sub-period owing to the fact that a very small area is available for excavation' (p. 41), and 'No street as such could be traced owing to the limited operations' (p. 42). What he did find was house platforms and kiln-brick drains from the first Harappan phase onward: 'the Harappans built their houses on platforms as early as Phase I of Sub-period II A as a precaution against inundation', raising them after each flood (p. 41). Phase I structures are a public drain of kiln-burnt bricks in RGP 3, a mud-brick room and verandah in RGP 4, and a mud-brick platform laid in layer 13 of RGP 7 (pp. 42-43). Sub-period II A has four structural phases in 8 ft. of deposit; Sub-period II B built no mud-brick structures or drains, and house platforms and drains were 'unknown' in II C (p. 42).
parts.excavator_basis: Cross-dating and a stratigraphic estimate, with no radiocarbon from Rangpur: 'There is no definite datable evidence from Rangpur itself' (p. 25). Rao takes the third flood at Lothal, 'dated 2000 B.C.' by the Lothal carbon-14 dates, as the time when Harappans came to Rangpur, so that 'the first Harappan settlement at Rangpur in Sub-period II A took place in 2000 B.C.', and allows about five centuries for the 10 ft. of II A debris, ending it with a flood 'in circa 1500 B.C.' (pp. 15, 25-26). The section drawing labels II A '2000 B.C.-1500 B.C.' (p. 14, fig. 3).

syntheses.statement: Possehl and Raval treat Rangpur II A as the Mature, Urban Phase in Saurashtra and Rangpur II B-C and III as the Post-urban sequence, and write that the earliest Rojdi pottery, Rojdi A, 'is quite similar to the pottery of Rangpur IIA'; they date Rojdi A to 2500-2200 B.C. by calibrated radiocarbon (p. 171).
syntheses.disagreement: By this ceramic parallel Rangpur II A would begin some centuries before Rao's 2000 B.C.; Possehl and Raval do not give a date for Rangpur itself.

syntheses.statement: Kanungo and colleagues write that 'Rangpur-IIA and IIB are placed under the Urban phase, and Rangpur-II C and Rangpur-III are under the Post-Urban', citing Possehl 1980, 1992, Possehl and Mehta 1994 and Rao 1963.
syntheses.disagreement: Rao 1963 puts II B (1500-1100 B.C.) after the flood that ended the mature settlement, as a degenerate phase; the later scheme puts it in the Urban phase.

parts.conflicts: Rao's dates were fixed before any radiocarbon date existed for Rangpur and are tied to his Lothal flood chronology; the later Gujarat syntheses we read move Rangpur II A into the Urban Phase of the later third millennium B.C. on ceramic grounds without new dates from the site. We found no radiocarbon determination from Rangpur in the Tata Institute, Physical Research Laboratory, Birbal Sahni or Pennsylvania lists, in Ramachandran 1975 or in Possehl and Raval 1989.

first_occupation.phase: Period I, pre-pottery microlithic culture (first Harappan occupation: Sub-period II A)
first_occupation.basis: Rao separates Period I from the Harappan Sub-period II A by a sterile silt and says that 'to guess a date is risky. However, provisionally the microlithic culture may be said to have flourished in 3000 B.C.' (p. 26). The first Harappan settlement, Sub-period II A, he dates to 2000 B.C. by cross-dating with Lothal (pp. 25-26).

sources.citation: Rao, S. R. 1963. Excavation at Rangpur and other explorations in Gujarat. Ancient India 18-19: 5-207 (summary pp. 13-19, chronology pp. 25-26, structures pp. 41-45). Image-only scan; printed page = PDF page - 13 for pp. 11-27 and PDF page - 23 for pp. 35-45.
Possehl, G. L. and Raval, M. H. 1989. Harappan Civilization and Rojdi. Leiden: E. J. Brill; New Delhi: Oxford & IBH.

Kanungo, A. K., Kaushal, R. K., Bhushan, R., Chauhan, N., Kharakwal, J. S. and Ansari, S. 2025. Luminescence and radiocarbon chronology of Bhagatrav: a Sorath Harappan camp site in South Gujarat. Radiocarbon 67: 53-73. doi:10.1017/RDC.2024.119

notes: Rangpur, on the Bhadar in Surendranagar district, was excavated by S. R. Rao for the Archaeological Survey of India for two seasons from December 1953 (p. 13; the section in fig. 3 is headed 1953-56), after earlier work by Vats, Ghurye and Dikshit. Rao's sequence is Period I (pre-pottery microlithic), Period II with Sub-periods II A (mature Harappan, structural Phases I-IV), II B and II C (late Harappan) and Period III (Lustrous Red Ware). We include Rangpur because Rao describes Harappan house platforms and burnt-brick drains from the first Harappan phase, Phase I of II A; it has no fortification and no traced street plan, and the excavation was a vertical dig in nine cuttings, so this is the weakest kind of layout evidence in the table. No radiocarbon date from Rangpur appears in any list or compilation we searched, and no Bayesian model exists. We read the report as page images; its text layer is empty.
